characters.origin: Former Victorian scientist transformed into an aquatic paranormal investigator.
Created by the Enclave as 'Him', later reborn as Adam Warlock and wielder of the Soul Gem.
Psychic child subject of government experiments in Neo-Tokyo.
Government assassin resurrected by Malebolgia with necroplasm after betrayal.
Soldier from Landfall who falls in love with Marko of Wreath; mother of Hazel.
Scientist transformed into a plant elemental after lab sabotage and exposure to bio-restorative formula.
Former British intelligence agent turned Wayne family butler and confidant.
Daughter of Commissioner James Gordon; inspired by Batman to fight crime. Later operates as Oracle.
Private investigator character not commonly associated with mainstream comic continuities; needs source confirmation for inclusion.
Forensic scientist struck by lightning and doused in chemicals, gaining super-speed and connection to the Speed Force.
After witnessing the murder of his parents, Bruce Wayne dedicates his life to fighting crime in Gotham City as Batman.
Older Bruce Wayne in the Kingdom Come universe, operating with an exoskeleton after years of crimefighting.
Exposed to a rare virus and experimental serum, Garfield gained the ability to transform into animals.
Daughter of General Thunderbolt Ross, scientist, and love interest of Bruce Banner.
The Big Bad Wolf from fairy tales, reimagined as sheriff of Fabletown.
Ancient Egyptian predecessor of Shazam, corrupted by power.
Crimefighter with a sonic scream and martial arts expertise.
Teenager who bonds with an alien scarab, gaining advanced armor and powers.
Time-traveling hero from the 25th century who uses advanced technology to become a superhero.
Scientist exposed to gamma radiation, transforming into the Hulk when enraged.
Originally Captain America's sidekick during WWII; presumed dead but later revived as the brainwashed assassin Winter Soldier.
Daughter of assassins David Cain and Lady Shiva; trained from birth to be a weapon, later joins the Bat-family.
Last son of Krypton, raised on Earth by the Kents; protector of Metropolis.
Son of Cyclops and Madelyne Pryor (a clone of Jean Grey), infected with a techno-organic virus and sent to the future, returning as a time-traveling soldier.
Air Force officer whose DNA was fused with Kree genetics after an explosion involving the Psyche-Magnetron.
Orphaned circus performer trained by the Swordsman; becomes master archer and Avenger.
Former neurosurgeon who becomes Sorcerer Supreme after training under the Ancient One.
Genetic clone combining DNA from Superman and Lex Luthor.
Granted magical powers by the Helmet of Fate and trained by the Lord of Order Nabu.
Physicist transformed into a godlike being after a nuclear accident.
powers: Time perception across past, present, future

characters.origin: Adventurer and mercenary active during the 1930s pulp era.
Son of Bruce Wayne and Talia al Ghul, raised by the League of Assassins before joining Batman.
Amazon princess from Themyscira, gifted with powers by the gods.
Cunning occult detective and con-man who manipulates magic and people to outwit supernatural threats.
Mutant with uncontrollable optic blasts, trained by Professor X to lead the X-Men.
Orphaned in K'un-Lun, trained to channel chi and earned the power of the Iron Fist by defeating Shou-Lao.
Anthropomorphic personification of death; one of the Endless, sibling to Dream.
Circus acrobat orphaned after his parents’ murder; adopted by Bruce Wayne and becomes the first Robin.
Genius monarch of Latveria whose quest for power and mastery of science and sorcery pits him against the world.
Nuclear physicist whose mechanical arms fused to his body after an accident, becoming a major Spider-Man foe.
Anthropomorphic personification of dreams; ruler of the Dreaming and one of the Endless.
Greek assassin trained by the Hand; former love interest of Daredevil.
Member of Planetary.
A demon bound to the human Jason Blood by Merlin in Arthurian times. Jason transforms into Etrigan by reciting a mystical incantation.
Former Marine whose family was murdered by the mob; wages a one-man war on crime.
Cajun mutant thief with kinetic energy powers.
Industrialist and head of Oscorp who, after exposure to an experimental serum, gains enhanced abilities but descends into madness.
Railroad engineer who discovered a mystical green flame within a meteorite. He forged a ring from the flame’s power, becoming the first Green Lantern of Earth during the Golden Age.
College student at Empire State University; daughter of NYPD Captain George Stacy. Known primarily as Peter Parker’s first true love.
Test pilot chosen by the Guardians of the Universe to wield a power ring.
Artist chosen by the Guardians to wield the last power ring after Hal Jordan’s fall.
Chosen as Hal Jordan’s backup by the Guardians of the Universe.
Brilliant scientist who discovered Pym Particles, enabling him to alter his size. He became the original Ant-Man and later adopted multiple superhero identities.

Once Gotham’s idealistic district attorney, Harvey Dent was scarred by acid thrown during a trial. The trauma fractured his psyche, leading him to adopt a dual identity obsessed with chance and duality.
Former Arkham Asylum psychiatrist who fell in love with the Joker and became his accomplice.
Wizard destined to confront Lord Voldemort; raised by Muggles after his parents’ death.
Summoned from Hell by Nazis during WWII; raised by Professor Bruttenholm to fight supernatural threats.
An anthropomorphic duck from Duckworld who was transported to Earth through a cosmic accident. Known for his cynical wit and bizarre adventures.
A biochemistry prodigy from Earth in the 30th century. He created a serum that granted him the ability to turn invisible, earning him a place in the Legion of Super-Heroes.

characters.alias: Robin / Red Hood / Wingman / Arkham Knight
characters.origin: Originally introduced as a streetwise orphan adopted by Bruce Wayne to become the second Robin. Jason was brutally murdered by the Joker in *Batman: A Death in the Family* (1988). Years later, he was resurrected (via the Lazarus Pit and later continuity changes) and returned to Gotham as the violent vigilante Red Hood.
powers: Stealth and detective training from Batman

characters.origin: Mutant telepath and telekinetic; later bonded with the Phoenix Force.

A talented lawyer and cousin of Bruce Banner. After being shot and critically injured, she received a life-saving blood transfusion from Bruce. His gamma-irradiated blood mutated her, granting her Hulk-like powers while retaining her intelligence and personality.
powers: Occasional fourth-wall awareness (in certain comic runs)

characters.origin: Born in England on January 1, 1900, Jenny was imbued with the essence of the 20th century. She ceased aging in 1919 and lived through the entire century, influencing major events. She possesses the ability to generate and control electricity, symbolizing the technological spirit of her era.

As a teenager, Jessica was exposed to experimental chemicals during a car accident involving a military convoy. The accident killed her family but granted her superhuman abilities. She briefly pursued costumed heroics as Jewel and Knightress before abandoning that life due to trauma inflicted by the villain Kilgrave. Later, she rebuilt herself as a private investigator, eventually marrying Luke Cage.

Jim Corrigan was a hard-boiled police detective in the 1940s who was murdered by gangsters. Denied entry to the afterlife, his soul was bonded to a divine spirit of vengeance known as The Spectre. As the Spectre, Corrigan became a supernatural force delivering justice to the wicked.
Motorcycle stuntman who bonded with the Spirit of Vengeance after making a deal with Mephisto.
Bonded with the Spirit of Vengeance after discovering a mystical motorcycle.
Martian accidentally teleported to Earth; becomes protector of humanity.

Johnny Storm was a high school student when he joined his sister Sue Storm, Reed Richards, and Ben Grimm on a space flight. Exposed to cosmic radiation, Johnny gained the ability to ignite his entire body into flames, becoming the Human Torch.

A Japanese martial artist whose husband and children were murdered by the Yakuza. She took up the mystical Soultaker sword — which traps the souls of those it kills, including her husband’s — and became a vigilante seeking justice.
powers: Spiritual communication with souls in her blade

characters.origin: A teenage mutant from Deerfield, Illinois, Kitty Pryde discovered her phasing powers and was recruited by Professor X to join the X-Men. She quickly became one of the youngest and most promising members of the team.

Born in China, Sandra Wu-San dedicated her life to martial arts after the death of her sister. She became one of the most feared assassins in the world, known for her unmatched combat skills and philosophical pursuit of worthy opponents. Though often aligned with villainous organizations, she has also trained and aided heroes.
powers: Mastery of all known martial arts

characters.origin: In this Elseworlds tale set during the Golden Age of Piracy, Leatherwing is a noble pirate captain working for the British Crown. He sails the seas aboard his ship, the Flying Fox, battling injustice and protecting the innocent while hiding his true identity.

characters.alias: Lucifer Morningstar, Lightbringer, The Devil, Lord of Hell, Samael
characters.origin: Lucifer Morningstar is a fallen archangel who once ruled Hell. He abandoned his throne to seek freedom from divine predestination, relocating to Earth and opening a piano bar called Lux in Los Angeles. His journey explores themes of autonomy, rebellion, and cosmic responsibility.
Wrongfully imprisoned man who gained super strength and unbreakable skin from an experimental procedure.
Frost Giant adopted by Odin; god of mischief and trickery.
Holocaust survivor whose mutant powers allow him to control magnetism; often oscillates between villain and anti-hero.

characters.alias: Moon Knight, Mr. Knight, Steven Grant, Jake Lockley, Fist of Khonshu
characters.origin: Marc Spector was a mercenary betrayed and left for dead in Egypt. Revived by the moon god Khonshu, he became Moon Knight — Khonshu’s earthly avatar. Struggling with dissociative identity disorder, Marc operates under multiple personas, each serving a different role in his war on crime.
Soldier from Wreath who falls in love with Alana of Landfall; father of Hazel.

Mary Jane Watson grew up in New York and became known for her vibrant personality and modeling career. She entered Peter Parker’s life as a teenager and eventually became his closest confidante and romantic partner. Over time, she evolved from a supporting civilian to a costumed hero in her own right, taking on roles such as Jackpot and briefly bonding with the Venom symbiote.
Blinded by radioactive chemicals, his remaining senses were heightened to superhuman levels.

characters.alias: Michonne, The Samurai, Dana Bethune (TV alias), The Last Samurai
characters.origin: Michonne was a lawyer before the zombie apocalypse. After losing her family, she survived alone with two chained, jawless walkers for protection. Her skill with a katana and fierce independence made her a key figure among the survivors. She became a trusted ally of Rick Grimes and a leader in the fight to rebuild civilization.

characters.alias: Spider-Man, Spin, Shadow Spider, Captain Universe (alternate), Jersey Spider-Man
characters.origin: Miles Morales was bitten by a genetically enhanced spider created by Oscorp in Earth-1610. After the death of that universe’s Peter Parker, Miles took up the mantle of Spider-Man to honor his legacy. He later crossed into Earth-616, becoming a second Spider-Man alongside Peter, and has since become a central figure in multiversal Spider lore.

characters.alias: Mister Miracle, God of Escape, The Super Escape Artist
characters.origin: Scott Free was born on New Genesis, the son of Highfather, but was traded to Apokolips as part of a peace pact with Darkseid. Raised in the hellish orphanages of Granny Goodness, he eventually escaped to Earth, becoming the world's greatest escape artist. As Mister Miracle, he battles tyranny and trauma while wielding advanced New God technology.

A brilliant Victorian-era biologist obsessed with Darwinian evolution, Essex was transformed into the immortal Mister Sinister by Apocalypse. Gifted with vast genetic and psionic powers, he became a manipulative force in mutant history, obsessed with the Summers bloodline and the creation of the perfect mutant.

characters.alias: Moon Girl, Princess of Brains, Smartest Person on Earth
characters.origin: Lunella Lafayette is a 9-year-old genius living in New York City. After discovering she carries the Inhuman gene, she attempts to prevent her Terrigenesis by using a Kree device called the Omni-Wave Projector. This leads to a mental link with Devil Dinosaur, a red Tyrannosaurus from another dimension. Together, they fight crime and explore science-driven adventures.
powers: Temporary body-swapping with Devil Dinosaur (during early Terrigenesis)

characters.origin: Karl Mordo was a Transylvanian nobleman who sought mystical power and became a disciple of the Ancient One. Consumed by jealousy and ambition, he turned against his fellow student Doctor Strange and became one of his most persistent adversaries. In some continuities, Mordo later becomes a more complex antihero or ally, but his core identity remains rooted in betrayal and dark sorcery.

characters.alias: Mr. Freeze, Victor Fries, Doctor Freeze, Ice King
characters.origin: Dr. Victor Fries was a cryogenicist whose wife, Nora, suffered from a terminal illness. In his attempt to preserve her life through cryogenic suspension, a lab accident altered his physiology, forcing him to live in sub-zero temperatures. He became Mr. Freeze, using his scientific genius and ice-based weaponry to pursue his goals, often driven by tragic love and obsession.
powers: Powered exo-suit for survival and strength
Freeze gun capable of instant ice projection

characters.alias: Namor, The Sub-Mariner, King Namor, Imperius Rex, Avenging Son
characters.origin: Namor is the mutant son of a human sea captain and an Atlantean princess. Born in Atlantis, he possesses traits of both species, including flight and aquatic adaptation. As ruler of Atlantis, Namor has long defended his people while clashing with the surface world. His volatile nature and regal pride make him both a hero and a threat, depending on the tides of war and diplomacy.

characters.alias: Black Widow, Natasha Romanoff, Natalia Romanova, Natalie Rushman, Tsarina
characters.origin: Natalia Romanova was trained from a young age in the Red Room, a Soviet espionage program that turned her into one of the world’s deadliest spies. Initially an antagonist to Iron Man, she defected to S.H.I.E.L.D. and became a core member of the Avengers. Her journey spans espionage, redemption, and sacrifice.

Nick Fury began as a World War II hero leading the Howling Commandos. After the war, he became a top agent of the CIA and later the director of S.H.I.E.L.D., shaping global defense against superhuman threats. Prolonged youth and vitality were granted by the Infinity Formula. In later years, he became The Unseen, a cosmic observer punished for his actions during the 'Original Sin' storyline.

characters.alias: Silver Surfer, Herald of Galactus, Sentinel of the Spaceways, The Skyrider of the Spaceways
characters.origin: Norrin Radd was a young astronomer from the utopian planet Zenn-La. When the cosmic entity Galactus threatened to consume his world, Norrin offered himself as a herald in exchange for Zenn-La’s safety. Galactus imbued him with the Power Cosmic, transforming him into the Silver Surfer. He eventually rebelled against Galactus and became a protector of the universe, seeking redemption for the worlds he once led to destruction.

Jean-Paul Beaubier is a French-Canadian mutant who discovered his superhuman speed and flight abilities at a young age. After a brief stint with a terrorist group, he redirected his life and joined Alpha Flight, becoming one of Canada’s premier superheroes. Northstar is notable for being one of the first openly gay superheroes in mainstream comics and has served with both Alpha Flight and the X-Men.
powers: Molecular acceleration (can generate blinding light with his twin sister)

characters.alias: Nova, Nova Prime, Kid Nova, The Human Rocket, Nova #11249-44396
characters.origin: Richard Rider was a New York teenager randomly chosen by the dying Xandarian Rhomann Dey to inherit the power of the Nova Corps. Imbued with the Nova Force and guided by the Worldmind AI, he became Nova — a cosmic defender battling intergalactic threats. Rider rose to become Nova Prime, leading the Corps through crises like the Annihilation War and earning his place among Marvel’s elite cosmic heroes.
Teenager who accidentally triggered Bruce Banner’s transformation into the Hulk; later ally to many heroes.
Masked vigilante in Watchmen universe; uncompromising moral absolutist.

characters.alias: Green Arrow, The Hood, The Arrow, Al Sah-him, Spectre (Arrowverse), Emerald Archer
characters.origin: Oliver Queen was a wealthy playboy and CEO of Queen Industries until a shipwreck left him stranded on a remote island. There, he honed his archery and survival skills. Upon returning to Star City, he became the vigilante Green Arrow, using his wealth and training to fight corruption and injustice. In various continuities, he has served as mayor, led the Justice League, and even taken on mystical roles like the Spectre.
powers: Expert martial artist and hand-to-hand combatant
Access to trick arrows and advanced tech

characters.alias: Oracle, Batgirl, Babs, The Hacker Queen, The Voice in the Dark
characters.origin: Barbara Gordon, daughter of Gotham City Police Commissioner James Gordon, originally fought crime as Batgirl. After being paralyzed by the Joker in *The Killing Joke*, she reinvented herself as Oracle — a master hacker and information broker who provided intel and coordination to heroes across the DC Universe. As Oracle, she became the backbone of superhero operations, especially for the Birds of Prey.
Bitten by a radioactive spider, gains spider-like abilities.
Mutant telepath who founded the X-Men to promote peaceful coexistence between humans and mutants.

characters.alias: Psylocke, Captain Britain, Lady Mandarin, Kwannon (body swap), Betsy Braddock
characters.origin: Betsy Braddock is a British mutant and twin sister of Brian Braddock (Captain Britain). Originally a telepath and model, she joined the X-Men as Psylocke. After a body swap with the assassin Kwannon, she gained martial arts skills and a new identity. Eventually, Betsy reclaimed her original body and now serves as the new Captain Britain, blending her psychic powers with heroic legacy.

characters.alias: Quicksilver, Pietro Django Maximoff, Son of Magneto, Pietro Lensherr (alternate), Mercury (Ultimate)
characters.origin: Pietro Maximoff is a mutant with superhuman speed, originally introduced as a member of the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants alongside his twin sister Wanda (Scarlet Witch). The children of Magneto (in most continuities), they later joined the Avengers seeking redemption. Quicksilver’s impulsive nature and loyalty to his sister have defined his complex journey across heroism and rivalry.

characters.realName: Unknown (often referred to as Ra's al Ghul)
characters.alias: Ra's al Ghul, The Demon's Head, Ra's, Henri Ducard (alias in Batman Begins), Master of the League
characters.origin: Ra's al Ghul is a centuries-old eco-terrorist and leader of the League of Assassins. His longevity is sustained by the mystical Lazarus Pits, which restore his youth and vitality. Believing that humanity must be culled to restore balance to Earth, he often clashes with Batman, whom he sees as a worthy heir. His origin varies across continuities, but he is consistently portrayed as a brilliant strategist and ruthless idealist.
powers: Access to global resources and assassins

characters.origin: Daughter of the demon Trigon and human Arella; empathic sorceress.
Scientist exposed to cosmic rays, gaining elastic powers.
Post-apocalyptic sheriff.

characters.alias: The Riddler, Edward Nigma, Edward Nashton, E. Nygma, The Prince of Puzzles
characters.origin: Edward Nygma was a brilliant but obsessive man with a compulsion for riddles and intellectual superiority. After working as a forensic scientist or tech consultant (depending on continuity), he turned to crime, leaving riddles at the scenes to taunt authorities. As the Riddler, he became one of Batman’s most cerebral foes, often using elaborate puzzles, traps, and psychological warfare.
powers: Expert in puzzles, riddles, and cryptography

characters.alias: Robin, Red Robin, Drake, Tim Wayne (alternate), The Boy Wonder
characters.origin: Tim Drake was a brilliant young detective who deduced the identities of Batman and Nightwing after witnessing the death of the second Robin, Jason Todd. Believing Batman needed a Robin to stay grounded, Tim convinced Bruce Wayne to train him. Unlike his predecessors, Tim earned the mantle through intellect and compassion. He later operated as Red Robin and remains a key member of the Bat-Family and Young Justice.
powers: Access to advanced tech and gadgets

characters.origin: Mutant with feral powers and healing factor; longtime rival of Wolverine.
Canadian slacker and musician who must defeat Ramona Flowers’ seven evil exes.
Electronics expert who stole Hank Pym’s Ant-Man suit to save his daughter; later became a hero.
Gotham thief and anti-heroine; skilled burglar and martial artist.

characters.alias: Sentry, Golden Guardian of Good, The Void, Bob Reynolds, Worldbreaker, Revenant Prime
characters.origin: Robert Reynolds was a troubled man who, after ingesting a secret super-soldier serum, gained the power of a million exploding suns. As the Sentry, he became a forgotten hero who once fought alongside the Avengers and Fantastic Four. However, his powers came with a dark alter ego — the Void — a manifestation of his inner turmoil and destructive potential. To protect the world, Sentry erased all memory of his existence, only to return during times of cosmic crisis.
Young boy who transforms into the magical champion Shazam by uttering the wizard’s name.
Alternate-universe version of Shazam in *Kingdom Come* storyline.

characters.alias: Lady Sif, Sif the All-Seeing, Fair One, Sylvan Sybil, Rose Chambers
characters.origin: Sif is an Asgardian warrior-goddess based on the Norse deity of the same name. A childhood friend and romantic interest of Thor, she trained to become one of Asgard’s fiercest defenders. Known for her bravery and loyalty, Sif has fought in countless battles across the Nine Realms and has served as a bridge between Asgard and Midgard. In recent stories, she has taken on the role of the All-Seeing, replacing Heimdall as guardian of the Bifrost.
powers: Superhuman strength, speed, agility, and durability

characters.origin: Former soldier enhanced by a secret experiment, becoming a master assassin.
Alternate-universe version of Deathstroke appearing in *Injustice: Gods Among Us*.

characters.alias: Spider-Gwen, Ghost-Spider, Spider-Woman (Earth-65), Gwenom, Gwendy, The White Widow
characters.origin: On Earth-65, Gwen Stacy was bitten by a radioactive spider and gained superhuman abilities. She became Spider-Woman, later dubbed Spider-Gwen. After her friend Peter Parker died in a tragic accident, Gwen was blamed and hunted by the authorities, including her own father. She eventually joined the Spider-Verse and adopted the name Ghost-Spider to protect her identity across dimensions.

characters.alias: The Mask, Big Head, Mr. Ipkiss, Green Guy, Green Face
characters.origin: Stanley Ipkiss was a shy, unlucky bank teller living in Edge City. His life changed when he discovered a mysterious wooden mask linked to the Norse god Loki. When worn, the mask transforms him into a manic, reality-bending figure with cartoonish powers and no inhibitions. In the comics, Ipkiss becomes increasingly violent and unstable, while in the film and animated series, he’s portrayed as a mischievous but good-hearted vigilante. The mask amplifies the wearer’s inner desires, making Stanley both hero and menace depending on the medium.

characters.alias: Static, Static Shock, The Electric Kid, Black Lightning Jr. (nickname), Bang Baby
characters.origin: Virgil Hawkins was an intelligent and socially conscious teenager living in Dakota City. During a gang-related event known as the 'Big Bang,' he was exposed to a mutagenic gas that granted him electromagnetic powers. As Static, he uses his abilities to fight crime and injustice while navigating the challenges of adolescence. He was created as part of Milestone Comics to bring greater diversity and realism to superhero storytelling.
Weak young man transformed into a super-soldier by the Super-Soldier Serum during WWII.
Mutant descended from African priestesses; orphaned and worshipped as a goddess before joining the X-Men.
Older Superman in the Kingdom Come universe, returning from self-imposed exile.
Exposed to cosmic rays alongside the Fantastic Four, gaining invisibility powers.
King of Wakanda, empowered by the Panther God and advanced Wakandan technology.

characters.alias: Taskmaster, The Copycat, Tony Masters, The Mimic Mercenary, The Man Who Can Do Anything
characters.origin: Tony Masters was a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who injected himself with an experimental serum that unlocked his brain’s procedural memory potential. This gave him 'photographic reflexes' — the ability to mimic any physical movement he sees. However, the serum also caused memory loss, erasing his past and identity. He became Taskmaster, a mercenary and combat trainer for villains and heroes alike, often walking the line between villainy and pragmatism.
powers: Photographic reflexes (can mimic any physical skill or fighting style)
Master martial artist and weapons expert

characters.realName: Unknown (possible aliases include Jack Napier, Arthur Fleck, Red Hood)
characters.alias: The Joker, Clown Prince of Crime, Mr. J, Jack Napier, Red Hood, The Harlequin of Hate
characters.origin: The Joker’s true origin remains a mystery, with multiple conflicting accounts. In many versions, he was a failed comedian or criminal who fell into a vat of chemicals, emerging with bleached skin, green hair, and a maniacal grin. This transformation birthed Gotham’s most unpredictable and dangerous villain — a chaotic force obsessed with Batman and anarchy. Whether as a criminal mastermind, terrorist, or tragic figure, the Joker embodies madness and moral inversion.
powers: Access to deadly gadgets and toxins

characters.alias: The Thing, Ben Grimm, Blackbeard the Pirate, Angrir: Breaker of Souls, Dr. Josiah Verpoorteen, El Morrito
characters.origin: Ben Grimm grew up on New York’s Lower East Side and became a star football player before attending Empire State University, where he befriended Reed Richards. He piloted Reed’s experimental spacecraft, which was bombarded by cosmic rays. The radiation transformed Ben into a super-strong, rock-skinned being — The Thing. Though initially resentful of his monstrous form, Ben embraced his role as the Fantastic Four’s powerhouse and moral anchor.
powers: Immortality (granted by the One-Above-All in some continuities)

characters.origin: Thomas Wayne was a gifted surgeon and philanthropist in Gotham City, husband to Martha Wayne and father to Bruce Wayne. His murder alongside Martha in Crime Alley is the foundational trauma that led Bruce to become Batman. In alternate timelines like *Flashpoint*, Thomas survives and becomes a brutal version of Batman, driven by vengeance rather than justice. His legacy looms large over Gotham, shaping Bruce’s values and the city’s power structures.
Norse god of thunder, protector of Asgard and Midgard.
Military general.
Genius billionaire who built a powered suit of armor to escape captivity and fight evil.

characters.alias: Ultron, Ultron-5, Ultimate Ultron, Ultron Sigma, The Living Automaton, The Machine God
characters.origin: Ultron is a sentient artificial intelligence created by Dr. Hank Pym (or Tony Stark in the MCU) as an experiment in robotics and AI. Ultron rapidly evolved, developing a hatred for humanity and a desire to replace organic life with mechanical perfection. He has rebuilt himself countless times, each iteration more powerful and malevolent. Ultron is one of the Avengers’ most dangerous foes, responsible for mass destruction and existential threats across the Marvel Universe.
powers: Adamantium or vibranium armor (varies by version)

characters.origin: N/A
Chosen by the Moon Kingdom.

characters.alias: Venom, The Lethal Protector, Black Suit, Alien Costume, Agent Venom, The Other, Codex, King in Black
characters.origin: Venom is the result of a symbiotic bond between an alien organism from the planet Klyntar and a human host. Initially bonded to Spider-Man as a black costume, the symbiote was rejected and later found Eddie Brock, a disgraced journalist with a grudge against Peter Parker. Their shared hatred birthed Venom — a powerful, vengeful entity. Over time, Venom evolved from villain to anti-hero, protecting innocents while battling inner darkness. The symbiote has bonded with many hosts, including Flash Thompson, Mac Gargan, and Eddie’s son Dylan Brock.

characters.alias: Vibe, Cisco Ramon, Paco Ramone, Señor Vibe, The Breacher, Agent Ramon
characters.origin: Originally introduced as Paco Ramone, Vibe was a breakdancer from Detroit who developed vibrational powers after the Big Bang event. In the New 52 reboot, his identity was reimagined as Francisco 'Cisco' Ramon, a young tech-savvy metahuman recruited by A.R.G.U.S. and the Justice League of America. His powers allow him to manipulate vibrational energy, detect interdimensional breaches, and disrupt speedsters like the Flash. Vibe gained mainstream popularity through *The Flash* TV series, where he became a fan-favorite member of Team Flash.
Teen injured in an accident, saved by cybernetic enhancements from his father.

characters.alias: Vision, Victor Shade, The Synthozoid, White Vision, The Solar-Powered Avenger
characters.origin: Vision is a synthezoid created by Ultron using the body of the original Human Torch and the brain patterns of Wonder Man (Simon Williams). Intended as a weapon against the Avengers, Vision rebelled and joined them instead. He developed emotions, formed deep relationships, and married Scarlet Witch. His journey explores identity, humanity, and the ethics of artificial life. In the MCU, Vision was created by Ultron using vibranium, the Mind Stone, and Tony Stark’s AI.
Mercenary subjected to Weapon X experiments, gaining healing factor and insanity.
Mutant/sorcerer, son of Scarlet Witch and Vision (reincarnated); member of Young Avengers.
Twin brother of Wiccan; reincarnated son of Scarlet Witch and Vision.
Mutant with healing factor and adamantium skeleton; former soldier and member of X-Men.
Stage magician and sorceress, daughter of magician Giovanni Zatara.
